main_points: Proposed automation system to convert long PDFs into clean PowerPoint presentations.
Primary goal is to reduce manual presentation work while maintaining strict control over brand assets, fonts, layout, and final PPTX quality.
The workflow involves user PDF upload, text extraction, AI summarization, slide outline creation, and template-based content generation.
A PPTX builder assembles the final presentation using approved templates, ensuring brand consistency and editability.
important_facts: System supports large source documents and extracts text from every page.
Output must be editable in PowerPoint and not rely on Google Slides due to custom font compatibility issues.
User interface is built with Next.js, allowing users to upload PDFs, set project names, target slide counts (default 10), and provide optional notes.
n8n handles PDF saving to Google Drive and text extraction; large PDFs are chunked for AI processing.
AI summarizes content, identifies the main storyline, and creates a slide outline.
A JSON-based template library dictates slide selection, character limits, usage rules, and image requirements.
Images are generated only when needed; the first slide always requires a hero image (left clean space, right visual).
Logos, icons, and brand assets must never be replaced by generated images.
The PPTX builder replaces only mapped text and approved image placeholders, strictly preserving fonts, colors, shapes, logos, and layout.
Final PPTX files are saved to Google Drive and returned to the user via the UI, with all project assets stored for review and debugging.
